about: Materials of well-known buildings for the code art (method A, v2/layers/art_a.py), where the seeded rule would give a famous building a colour it does not have. One entry per ACT building id: facade (a palette buildings.facade_* name) or stone (true: yellow sandstone ashlar), and roof (a palette buildings.roof_* name). Everything else about the building (windows, surrounds, tone) follows the rule. Chosen by hand from public photographs; add a building here rather than changing the rule. kinds: the materials of a kind of building that the data tells (v2/data/scene/worship.py): the walls of a place of worship are stone and its windows are arched, round-headed unless the building's own entry says windows: pointed. A building's own facade or stone goes before its kind's. An entry with kind: place_of_worship makes a building one that OSM does not map as a church. clad: parts of the building covered in sheet metal, walls and roof alike (a copper spire with its lantern): each a name, the centre (E, N; LUREF) and radius (m) of an upright cylinder, the altitude it starts at (above, m) and a palette colour; what the model has of the building inside it is that colour, a material of its own.

clad.name: the central spire and its lantern, in copper gone green (the two tower spires are slate)
